must_have_features.feature: Consented brain that ingests everything continuously: calls (Zoom/Meet/Loom), DMs and email threads, SOPs, ad-account teardowns and course videos are ingested daily, transcribed with speaker labels, PII-redacted, deduplicated, owner-approved and versioned. A visible freshness stamp should target 24 hours or less behind the owner.
must_have_features.why: The brain is the moat; the competing creator says so himself (Aug 19, 2026). Jeremy AI claims 11,400+ call hours, 85,000+ DMs, 400+ SOPs and 1,200+ audits, synced daily. Operator AI is only as deep as inputs/ and has never run on a real archive. Call and DM archives contain third parties' personal data, so we need per-source consent and notice records and redaction. Without them, the biggest data advantage becomes a legal liability.

must_have_features.feature: Measurable persona fidelity: answers that read like Mbang. Build a style layer from his real written and spoken answers (phrasing, directness, recurring analogies) on top of cited retrieval. Run a standing blind test where team members and students who know him pick the real answer vs the AI answer, publish the score, and target near-chance. Regress-test on every model or prompt change.
must_have_features.why: 'Sounds exactly like Mbang' is the user's explicit bar. Jeremy AI markets 'the exact phrasing' and says people who know the creator find the answers indistinguishable, but publishes no measurement. A published fidelity score beats an anecdote, and it catches drift when models change. Citations must survive the style rewrite.

must_have_features.feature: Consented voice clone on a real phone number and in-app: Mbang records and verifies his own voice, can revoke it at any time, and turns run at sub-second latency. The line discloses that it is AI at the start of every call. Outbound AI-voice calls go only to people who gave prior express consent. A video-call mode is optional.
must_have_features.why: The creator reports that the phone demo drew the strongest response of his whole launch (Aug 19, 2026). Operator AI currently refuses to clone, so it loses parity on the most-loved feature; the fix is consent, not refusal. ElevenLabs Professional Voice Cloning lets you clone only your own voice and requires verification. FCC Declaratory Ruling 24-17 (released Feb 8, 2024) treats AI-generated voices as 'artificial' under the TCPA, which requires prior express consent. EU AI Act Art. 50 (applies from Aug 2, 2026) requires disclosure of AI interaction and labelling of synthetic audio.

must_have_features.feature: Every channel people already use: web/PWA, Telegram (DM plus group team mode), WhatsApp, SMS, Slack, phone, email, an embeddable widget for course and community pages, and an MCP server plus Claude/ChatGPT connectors. One memory and permission model across all of them.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI runs on Telegram, web, SMS, phone, groups and MCP, and power users already plug its MCP into their own agent harnesses. Kajabi ships an MCP. Apollo exposes agent tools over MCP. Delphi has no public MCP, which is an opening. Operator AI's senders are built but off. A channel that is switched off doesn't count.

must_have_features.feature: Persistent per-user business memory: each student's and each client's offer, niche, price, numbers, past decisions and prior answers. An editable 'what I know about you' panel, scoped per workspace, exportable and deletable.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI, BuddyPro, Utari and Circle AI all sell memory as the reason advice gets better over time. Advice that ignores last week's numbers is generic, and memory without user control is a privacy problem.

must_have_features.feature: No input limits and full multimodal intake: full call recordings and transcripts, long scripts, Ads Manager screenshots and CSV exports, funnel URLs, decks and PDFs are read in full, not truncated, with the cost shown to the owner.
must_have_features.why: The competing creator lists missing file uploads and a character limit among the reasons advanced users churned (Aug 19, 2026). Utari now sells 'no limits, any file type'. This is now the minimum, not an advantage.

must_have_features.feature: Approval-gated agents that act inside the real tools, live and not mocked. Targets: GoHighLevel first, then HubSpot; Meta and Google Ads (read, plus paused drafts with budget caps and rollback); Google/Outlook calendars; Stripe; Gmail/Outlook; Slack; Google Slides/Docs; page builders. Each action shows a diff preview with approve, edit or reject, has a configurable autonomy level per action type, can be undone, and is written to the audit log.
must_have_features.why: Answering without acting was the key limitation the competing creator named, and why he rebuilt on an agentic platform. Utari claims its clone runs ad accounts and edits CRMs, but documents no approvals or rollback. Delphi Actions offers confirm-before-act. Artisan offers approvals and locked tone. Operator AI's approval queue is its strongest differentiator, but every live switch is off and nothing has been sent for real. 'Fully real, no demo' means switching connectors on per tenant with these controls.

must_have_features.feature: Event-triggered workers with scoped knowledge. Examples: a new call transcript triggers a rubric audit and a drill assignment; a new lead is qualified and a reply drafted; a spend or CPL anomaly triggers a diagnosis; a student silent for 7 days gets a nudge and coach escalation; a failed payment triggers a dunning draft. Each worker sees only the knowledge and tools its job needs.
must_have_features.why: Utari's core engine is workers plus triggers plus per-worker knowledge scoping. Delphi Actions fire on messages, topics and tool signals. The value comes from work that starts without someone having to ask.

must_have_features.feature: Deliverables, not advice: build and stage ready-to-ship assets in the destination tool. That covers the webinar registration page, slide deck, a 48-72h show-up reminder stack, email and SMS sequences, VSL script, ad hooks and creative variants, setter and closer scripts, proposals and client reports. Each is traced to the frameworks it used and checked by the guardrails before approval.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI writes these as text. Its planned rebuild adds slides, landing pages and sequences. Kajabi Cofounder drafts product, offer, sales page and emails. GoHighLevel builds funnels from a prompt. To beat them, assets must land in the user's real tools already wired up, not as text to copy and paste.

must_have_features.feature: Webinar funnel operating system: plan, then assets, ads, registrations, show-up, live, replay, follow-up, calls and cash. Live metrics at every stage (cost per registration, show rate, booked-call rate, close rate, cash collected) feed a diagnostic that names the stage to fix next and drafts the fix.
must_have_features.why: The user explicitly wants best-in-class webinar ads and operations. Jeremy AI sells show-up stacks, webinar playbooks and cash-collected modelling as advice. Nobody runs the whole chain with stage-level numbers from connected sources.

must_have_features.feature: Sales role-play gym for students and team: voice (and optionally video) role-plays with AI prospects built from the programme's real objection library and each student's actual target niche. Scorecards follow the programme's own call framework, feedback is line by line, difficulty climbs a ladder, and there are leaderboards. A certification gate must be passed before a student may send real outreach or take live calls.
must_have_features.why: Hyperbound and Second Nature show that role-play plus scorecards plus certification is a category buyers pay for. None of the creator clones (Jeremy AI, Delphi, Coachvox, BuddyPro) trains people this way. Certification gating is also a safety control: untrained students don't get to email real prospects.

must_have_features.feature: Real call review and live call copilot: score recorded discovery and sales calls against the programme rubric, turn mistakes into assigned drills, and track improvement. An optional in-call assist suggests objection answers and next questions, with recording-consent capture where required.
must_have_features.why: Hyperbound Perform scores real calls and is previewing live coaching. Second Nature has Deal Coach. Utari's example worker audits sales calls. Jeremy AI was shown during live sales calls. Closing the practice-to-real-call loop is how training turns into revenue.

must_have_features.feature: 'First client' mission engine for growth operators: a staged, evidence-checked path from niche and offer, through ICP list, outreach, replies, booked calls, proposal, signed client and onboarding, to the first results report. Each step cites its SOP and sets daily targets. Blockers auto-flag to a coach, and the owner sees exactly where every student is stuck.
must_have_features.why: No competitor owns this end to end. Clones advise, SDR tools send, communities host, role-play tools train. This is the wedge that makes Operator AI the layer that replaces much of a growth-operator support team, and it gives the owner a retention and outcomes story without income promises.

must_have_features.feature: Prospecting and enrichment through integrations, not a home-built database: Apollo, Clay and Instantly data via the student's own keys or MCP, waterfall email verification, and signal-based lists (hiring, active ads, funding, site visitors). Dedupe and claim prospects across the whole cohort so two students never pitch the same business.
must_have_features.why: Apollo, Clay (Claygent plus waterfalls), Instantly (450M+ leads) and Artisan (250M+ contacts) already own data. Rebuilding it is waste. Cross-student dedupe is a programme-level need none of them solves, and it protects both prospects and the programme's reputation.

must_have_features.feature:
Compliant outreach on the student's behalf, held to each platform's rules:
- Email goes from the student's own authenticated domains and mailboxes (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, warm-up), with the spam rate monitored and kept under the 0.3% threshold, one-click unsubscribe on marketing mail, a shared suppression list, and volume caps.
- Instagram and Facebook replies are sent only inside Meta's messaging window, with an automated-chat disclosure.
- LinkedIn and other platforms that ban automation get a drafted message the student sends with one tap.
- AI-voice outbound calls go only to people with prior express consent.
must_have_features.why:
'Doing outreach on their behalf' is where these products can do the most damage:
- Gmail sender rules (in force since Feb 1, 2024) require authentication, a spam rate below 0.3% and one-click unsubscribe for bulk mail.
- Meta's Messenger policy limits standard messaging to a 24h window and requires bot disclosure where the law demands it.
- LinkedIn's 'Prohibited software and extensions' page bans automation tools.
- FCC 24-17 (Feb 8, 2024) covers AI voices.

Instantly advertises that campaigns run completely on autopilot, and 11x documents no approval step. Being compliant by construction is a real advantage, not overhead.

must_have_features.feature: Reply handling and booking: classify every reply (interested, objection, not now, unsubscribe, wrong person). Draft the response in the student's voice using programme-approved objection answers, offer calendar times, book the call, and send confirmations and show-up reminders. Humans approve every reply until that student's measured draft accuracy passes a set threshold, then autonomy rises per category.
must_have_features.why: Instantly's AI Reply Agent, GoHighLevel's AI Sales Agent and Voice AI booking, 11x and Delphi's demo-scheduling Action all compete here. Speed to lead decides who gets the meeting. Earned, measured autonomy beats either always-manual or always-autopilot.

must_have_features.feature: Verified outcome ledger: each student's and client's funnel numbers (sent, replies, booked, shows, closes, cash collected) are pulled from connected systems (CRM, Stripe, calendar, ad accounts), never self-reported. Cohort analytics show which SOPs, assets and behaviours correlate with results. An evidence pack can be exported to back any claim.
must_have_features.why: Every competitor's proof is unverified: BuddyPro claims 1,616% average ROI, Jeremy AI shows screenshot testimonials, and 11x and Second Nature publish vendor stats. FTC 'Operation AI Comply' (Sep 25, 2024) sued schemes that promised AI-powered income (Ascend Ecom, Ecommerce Empire Builders, FBA Machine) and said there is no AI exemption. Verified outcomes are the only defensible way to show the system makes people money.

must_have_features.feature: Claims and testimonial guard on everything the AI writes for the owner, team and students. It blocks unsubstantiated income or result claims, fake or AI-written testimonials, fake scarcity and undisclosed AI personas. Any results claim must link to an evidence record from the outcome ledger and carry a typical-results disclosure. Testimonials need a stored consent record.
must_have_features.why: The FTC's final rule on fake reviews and testimonials (announced Aug 14, 2024) bans AI-generated testimonials and testimonials from people who don't exist. Jeremy AI's marketing ('go get richer', 'one win covers the year') shows how normal this risk is in the niche. Operator AI already has income-claim and fake-proof guards. Extending them to require linked evidence turns a filter into a moat.

must_have_features.feature: Timestamped video citations: every answer drawn from a course video or call jumps to the exact second, plays the clip, and keeps document file-and-line citations. When the material doesn't cover the question, it says 'not covered'.
must_have_features.why: Kajabi now bundles a Teaching Assistant that answers with timestamped course clips in every plan. Cited Q&A over course content is now commodity, so file-and-line citations alone are no longer a differentiator. Jeremy AI and Delphi show no answer-level citations, so pairing precise video citations with honest 'not covered' answers still wins.

must_have_features.feature: Scoped instances and access groups as sales and delivery assets: one-click limited versions such as a webinar-attendee bot trained only on webinar content, a challenge bot, a prospect-facing sales assistant, and separate student and inner-circle tiers. Each has message or time caps, email-code access, abuse controls, an expiry date and an upgrade path, while the full course knowledge base stays private.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI used time-limited webinar and 3-day-challenge instances with message caps, email-code access and VPN blocking as funnel and retention tools (Aug 19, 2026). Delphi shipped Access Groups (Aug 19, 2025). Kajabi's Sales Agent answers buyers on the sales page. This turns the AI into the owner's top-of-funnel asset.

must_have_features.feature: Owner monetisation and white-label: the owner can sell the AI itself (subscription, trials, coupons, usage tiers, seats via Stripe or Whop). Students can deploy white-label sub-instances for their own clients, with revenue share, usage metering and licence locks that keep the course knowledge base private.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI is sold standalone at $1,000/month, with $60K+/month claimed. BuddyPro, Coachvox and Delphi sell AI subscriptions with trials and coupons. Utari plans white-label instances for students and clients. Smartlead charges $29/month per white-label client workspace, and GoHighLevel's SaaS mode lets agencies resell. Operator AI is already multi-tenant but has no billing or resale layer.

must_have_features.feature: Proactive accountability driven by real activity: check-ins over Telegram, WhatsApp or SMS fire on pipeline signals (no outreach sent, reply backlog, missed drills, no calls booked) rather than on a calendar. Quiet hours, opt-out and escalation to a human coach are built in.
must_have_features.why: BuddyPro's main hook is proactive check-ins on Telegram. Delphi Actions follow up at milestones. Nudges tied to actual pipeline data beat generic reminders, and they are how students reach a first client.

must_have_features.feature: Universal inbox with human takeover and handback across all channels. The AI identifies itself as AI and names the owner or coach rather than impersonating them by default; persona voice is used only where Mbang has consented and disclosure is in place.
must_have_features.why: Kajabi's Universal Inbox (read any chat, take over, hand back) and its honest AI identity set the bar. GoHighLevel and Instantly (Unibox) centralise replies. EU AI Act Art. 50 requires AI-interaction disclosure from Aug 2, 2026, and Meta's policy requires bot disclosure where the law demands it.

must_have_features.feature: Ad-account audits from live connections: read-only Meta and Google Ads with the owner's audit rules encoded. It catches issues such as an objective silently changed during duplication, a pixel optimising for unqualified leads, or spend not delivering. Fixes are staged as paused drafts with budget caps, approval and one-click rollback.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI's testimonials centre on exactly these catches, and it claims 1,200+ audits of training data. Utari claims its clone runs ad accounts. Operator AI audits CSV exports and has a real Meta client built but switched off. Live read access is required for parity, and paused-only writes make it safer than both.

must_have_features.feature: Speed and reliability targets, published and monitored: first text token in about 1 second or less, typical full answer within 2-3 seconds, voice turn latency under about 800ms, and 99.9% uptime. Graceful, labelled fallback when the model provider is down.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI markets answers in under 2 seconds. Slow answers kill daily habit, and habit drives retention of the AI subscription.

must_have_features.feature: Team mode with RBAC: cheap or unlimited seats, group-chat mode, and role workspaces (setter, closer, coach, media buyer, VA, student, client) with per-role tools and data permissions. Shared projects carry memory and hand-offs.
must_have_features.why: Jeremy AI sells Telegram group access so the whole team works from one playbook. Circle AI has shared projects with memory. Hyperbound and Second Nature give managers team analytics. Operator AI's 5-role RBAC is ahead, but it has to work inside the group chats people actually use.

must_have_features.feature: Security and data rights: a signed DPA, no training of third-party models on owner data, per-tenant encryption, SSO, full export and deletion, consent records for every archive used in training, and a SOC 2 roadmap.
must_have_features.why: Hyperbound is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. Utari publishes a DPA. Coachvox and BuddyPro promise no training on customer content. Delphi says the creator owns the data. Programme owners are uploading their entire IP plus clients' personal data, so this is table stakes.

must_have_features.feature: Multilingual text and voice: answer in the user's language, translate cited passages, and speak in the owner's consented voice across languages, with disclosure.
must_have_features.why: Utari advertises auto-translation and users in 100+ countries. Coachvox claims 50+ languages, Hyperbound 25+ and Second Nature 30+. Delphi features a teacher's mind available 'in any language' (Mar 18, 2026). Operator AI detects only FR/ES/PT today.

must_have_features.feature: Lead-magnet and distribution kit for the owner: export approved frameworks as downloadable agent-skill files and a public MCP/connector, plus email-gated 'ask the AI' demo pages that feed the sales funnel and the scoped-instance upsell. Licence terms are applied to everything exported.
must_have_features.why: The competing creator turned 38 public agent-skill files into an email-gated lead magnet that led to the AI's sales page (skills synced Mar 30, 2026; funnel described Aug 19, 2026). Kajabi ships an MCP. Distribution decides adoption.

must_have_features.feature: Community-platform presence: a bot or embed inside Skool, Circle, Kajabi, Mighty and Telegram groups, with membership and progress synced so access follows the student's tier.
must_have_features.why: Coaching programmes live in these communities. Delphi published a community-integration guide (Dec 10, 2025), Coachvox embeds anywhere, Kajabi and Circle have native AI, and Skool auto-DMs new members. Making students go to a separate app costs adoption.

must_have_features.feature: Owner intelligence console: what students ask (content gaps that suggest new modules), unanswered or 'not covered' rates, grounding and fidelity eval scores, AI cost per user, and revenue by AI tier.
must_have_features.why: Delphi Insights, Coachvox audience insights and Circle's Data Explorer show buyers expect this. Operator AI's eval and Command Centre pages are a strong base. Exposing gaps and fidelity drift is how the owner keeps the brain improving.

must_have_features.feature: Consented video avatar of the owner for role-plays and Q&A, optionally joining Zoom or Meet as a participant, with an on-screen AI label.
must_have_features.why: Tavus agents join Zoom, Meet and Teams on camera. Second Nature sells avatar role-plays. Jeremy AI reportedly had a video call at launch. It is a strong demo but not core to producing results.
